newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.09 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.09 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.09 percent to end at 1.0285 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency at 1.0285 to 1.0335 per dollar, dealers said.

The Central Bank set the new trading level for the fluctuation of the real by buying dollars at 1.0285 real and selling at 1.0335 reais at a morning auction. The move was expected by the market, dealers said.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Thursday surplus of around $75 million.
The Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0285 real per U.S. unit to drain excess dollars from the market and maintain the new mini-band in the late afternoon.
The previous mini-band, set on November 1, was between 1.0275 and 1.0325 reais to the dollar.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real also dropped 0.09 percent to end at 1.0340 to the dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed steady at 1.075 per greenback, traders said.
